children: Commodity markets traded mixed on November 6, with oil prices heading for their biggest weekly decline since April while gold was set for its biggest weekly gain since August as a weaker dollar and lower US Treasury yields boosted demand for the precious metal.
Oil was on track for the biggest weekly loss since April after a volatile stretch of trading, as investors weighed prospects for an end to the months-long war in the Middle East.
West Texas Intermediate rose to trade near $91 a barrel on Friday, extending a rebound from a sharp selloff following a
Democratic sweep of the US midterm elections. Still, prices are down more than 12% this week.
Gold was on track for its biggest weekly gain since August after the US midterm elections sent the dollar and Treasury yields lower.
Bullion traded around $4,090 an ounce, on track for a weekly advance of more than 5%.
Among other precious metals, silver was 0.4% higher at $51.99. Platinum and palladium edged lower.

The dollar held steady against major currencies on Friday, after a sharp selloff in US equities drove investors toward haven assets such as the yen and pushed Treasury yields lower ahead of a closely watched government payrolls report.

title: Commodity Corner: Oil set for biggest weekly fall since April; gold eyes best week since August
